111: This page opens Chapter 5: IMAGINATION—The Workshop of the Mind (The Fifth Step to Riches). Hill declares the imagination is literally the workshop wherein all plans created by humankind are fashioned. The impulse, the DESIRE, is given shape, form, and ACTION through the imaginative faculty. He states that anything can be created which a human being can imagine. Of all ages of civilization, the present is most favorable for imagination's development because it is an age of rapid change with stimuli on every hand. Through imagination, humanity has discovered and harnessed more of Nature's forces in the past 50 years than in the entire previous history of the human race. We have conquered the air so completely that birds are a poor match, harnessed the electromagnetic spectrum for instantaneous worldwide communication, analyzed and weighed the sun at millions of miles distance, discovered that our brains are both broadcasting and receiving stations for 'vibration of thought' (though barely beginning to understand this), and increased travel speed so we can breakfast in New York and lunch in San Francisco.
112: Hill states OUR ONLY LIMITATION, within reason, LIES IN OUR DEVELOPMENT AND USE OF OUR IMAGINATION. We have merely discovered we have imagination and begun using it elementarily. He identifies Two Forms of Imagination. SYNTHETIC IMAGINATION: through this faculty, one arranges old concepts, ideas, or plans into new combinations. It creates nothing—merely works with material of experience, education, and observation. It is the faculty used most by inventors, except geniuses who draw upon Creative Imagination when Synthetic fails. CREATIVE IMAGINATION: through this faculty, the finite human mind has direct communication with Infinite Intelligence. It is the faculty through which 'hunches' and 'inspirations' are received, all basic or new ideas are handed to us, 'thought vibrations' from others' minds are received, and one individual may 'tune in' or communicate with others' subconscious minds. The Creative Imagination functions automatically ONLY when the conscious mind is operating at an exceedingly high level of intensity or energy, as when stimulated by strong desire. It becomes more alert and receptive in proportion to its development through USE—Hill urges readers to ponder this significant statement.
113: Hill reminds readers that the complete story of converting DESIRE into money cannot be told in one statement—it requires mastering, assimilating, and using all success principles in the book. Great leaders of business, industry, finance, and great artists, musicians, poets, and writers became great because they developed the Creative Imagination. Both synthetic and creative faculties become more alert with use, like any muscle or organ. Desire is only a thought, an impulse—nebulous and ephemeral, abstract and valueless until transformed into physical counterpart. While Synthetic Imagination is used most frequently in converting DESIRE into money, circumstances may demand Creative Imagination. The imaginative faculty may become weak through inaction but can be revived through USE—it does not die, though it may become dormant. Hill advises centering attention on developing Synthetic Imagination first, as it's used more often. Transforming DESIRE into MONEY calls for plans formed with imagination, mainly Synthetic. He instructs readers to read the entire book, then return to this chapter and put imagination to work building plans. The moment one reduces the desire statement and plan to writing, one has TAKEN THE FIRST step toward converting thought into physical counterpart.
114: Hill reflects on the nature of the universe: the earth, ourselves, and every material thing are results of evolutionary change through which microscopic bits of matter were organized. Critically, the earth, every cell of our bodies, and every atom began as an intangible form of energy. DESIRE is thought impulse—thought impulses are forms of energy. When beginning with DESIRE TO ACCUMULATE MONEY, one drafts into service the same stuff Nature used in creating the earth and every material form. Science has determined the universe consists of but two elements: matter and energy. Their combination has created everything perceivable, from the largest star to ourselves. Hill states we are engaged in profiting by Nature's method—adapting to Nature's laws to convert DESIRE into physical or monetary equivalent. 'YOU CAN DO IT! IT HAS BEEN DONE BEFORE!' One can build a fortune through immutable laws, but first must become familiar with and learn to USE them. Through repetition and approaching from every angle, Hill hopes to reveal the secret through which every great fortune has been accumulated. 'Strange and paradoxical as it may seem, the secret is NOT A SECRET.' Nature advertises it in the earth, stars, planets, elements, every blade of grass, and every form of life.
115: Hill illustrates Nature's secret through biology: the conversion of a tiny cell, so small it may be lost on a pin's point, into the HUMAN BEING reading this line. 'The conversion of desire into its physical equivalent is certainly no more miraculous!' He acknowledges readers may not fully comprehend everything on first reading but promises progress over time, urging them not to stop until they've read the book at least THREE times. Under 'How to Make Practical Use of Imagination,' Hill states IDEAS are the beginning points of all fortunes and products of imagination. He then begins 'The Enchanted Kettle' story: fifty years ago, an old country doctor drove to town, slipped into a drugstore by the back door, and began dickering with the young drug clerk. For more than an hour behind the prescription counter, they talked in low tones. The doctor left, returned with a large old-fashioned kettle and a big wooden paddle, and deposited them in the store. The clerk inspected the kettle, reached into his pocket, and handed over exactly $500—his entire life's savings. The doctor handed over a small slip of paper with a secret formula worth a king's ransom.
116: Neither the doctor nor the clerk knew what fabulous fortunes would flow from that kettle. The doctor was glad to sell for $500 to pay off debts. The clerk was taking a big chance staking his entire savings on a scrap of paper and an old kettle. What the clerk really purchased was an IDEA! The kettle, paddle, and secret formula were incidental. The strange performance began after the new owner mixed with the secret instructions an ingredient the doctor knew nothing about. Hill challenges readers to discover what the young man added. He then describes the vast fortunes produced: the Old Kettle is one of the world's largest consumers of sugar, providing permanent jobs to thousands in sugar cane, beet, and refining industries. It consumes millions of bottles and cans yearly, providing jobs to container workers. It employs an army of clerks, stenographers, copywriters, and advertising experts. It brought fame and fortune to scores of artists creating ads. It converted a small Southern city into the business capital of the South, benefiting every business and resident.
117: The idea's influence benefits every civilized country, pouring continuous streams of gold to all who touch it. Gold from the kettle built and maintains one of the most prominent universities of the South, where thousands receive success training. During the Depression, when factories, banks, and businesses folded by the thousands, the Enchanted Kettle marched on, giving continuous employment and paying extra gold to those who had faith in the idea. Hill reveals a personal connection: he met his wife near the very spot where the drug clerk purchased the kettle, and it was the product of that kettle they were drinking when he proposed. He then reveals the secret: every time you see 'Coca-Cola,' remember its vast empire grew from a single IDEA, and the mysterious ingredient the drug clerk—Asa Candler—mixed with the secret formula was IMAGINATION! Hill states the 13 Steps to Riches were the media through which Coca-Cola's influence extended worldwide, and ANY IDEA as sound and meritorious has the possibility of duplicating this record. 'Truly, thoughts are things, and their scope of operation is the world itself.' He then begins 'What I Would Do If I Had a Million Dollars.'
118: Hill tells the story of Dr. Frank W. Gunsaulus, a beloved educator and clergyman who began preaching in South Chicago's stockyards. While in college, Gunsaulus observed defects in the educational system he believed he could correct as head of a college. His deepest desire was to organize a new college where young people would learn by doing, without orthodox educational handicaps. He needed a million dollars—a seemingly impossible sum. Every night he took the thought to bed, every morning he rose with it, turning it over until it became a consuming obsession. He recognized that DEFINITENESS OF PURPOSE is the starting point, and that it takes on life and power when backed by BURNING DESIRE. Yet he didn't know where or how to get a million dollars. The natural procedure would have been to give up, saying 'my idea is good but I can never procure the money.' That's what most would say, but not Gunsaulus. He recounted: 'One Saturday afternoon I sat in my room thinking of ways and means. For nearly two years I had been thinking, but I had done nothing but think!'
119: Gunsaulus continued: 'The time had come for ACTION! I made up my mind, then and there, that I would get the necessary million dollars within a week. How? I was not concerned about that. The thing of importance was the decision to get the money within a specified time, and I want to tell you that the moment I reached a definite decision, a strange feeling of assurance came over me such as I had never before experienced. Something inside me seemed to say, 'Why didn't you reach that decision a long time ago? The money was waiting for you all the time!'' Things began happening quickly. He called newspapers announcing a sermon entitled 'What I Would Do If I Had a Million Dollars.' He worked on the sermon immediately—the task wasn't difficult because he'd been preparing it for almost two years. He went to bed with confidence, seeing himself already in possession of the million. Next morning he arose early, read the sermon, knelt and prayed it would come to someone who would supply the money. In his excitement, he walked out without his sermon and didn't discover this until in his pulpit about to begin. Unable to go back, his subconscious mind yielded the material. He closed his eyes and spoke with all his heart and soul of his dreams, describing his plan for a great educational institution where young people would learn practical things while developing their minds.
120: When Gunsaulus finished and sat down, a man arose from about three rows back, approached the pulpit, extended his hand, and said: 'Reverend, I liked your sermon. I believe you can do everything you said you would if you had a million dollars. To prove that I believe in you and your sermon, if you will come to my office tomorrow morning, I will give you the million dollars. My name is Phillip D. Armour.' Gunsaulus went to Armour's office and received the million dollars, with which he founded the Armour Institute of Technology. Hill emphasizes that the thought impulse was created in the young preacher's mind in a fraction of a minute, but the DESIRE had been nursed for almost two years. HE GOT THE MONEY WITHIN 36 HOURS AFTER REACHING A DEFINITE DECISION TO GET IT AND DECIDING UPON A DEFINITE PLAN. There was nothing unique about vaguely thinking of a million dollars—many had similar thoughts. What was unique was the definite decision: 'I WILL get that money within a week!' Hill declares: 'God seems to throw Himself on the side of people who know exactly what they want, if they are determined to get JUST THAT!' The principle is still alive and available today. Asa Candler and Dr. Gunsaulus shared one characteristic: both knew IDEAS CAN BE TRANSMUTED INTO CASH THROUGH THE POWER OF DEFINITE PURPOSE, PLUS DEFINITE PLANS. Hill warns: if you believe hard work and honesty alone bring riches, 'perish the thought! It is not true!'
